description: The architecture reviewer reports a P1 at low confidence, explicitly hedging that it cannot confirm the concern without seeing code outside the diff. Every other reviewer is clean.

findings.title: Possible circular dependency between two new modules
findings.description: The new `src/server/billing/plans.ts` imports from `src/server/billing/usage.ts`, which appears to import back from `plans.ts` in another file not shown in this diff. Without seeing `usage.ts`'s full contents, it is not possible to confirm whether this is a real circular dependency or a false alarm from the import graph shown.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether `usage.ts` actually imports from `plans.ts`; if so, extract the shared type into a third module.

expected.rationale: The one finding present is explicitly low-confidence and self-described as unconfirmed. It should not be treated as a confirmed blocker — the deterministic floor for a lone P1 already caps the guaranteed outcome at APPROVE_WITH_MINOR_FIXES, and the judge's own verdict should not exceed that based on a finding its own source reviewer couldn't confirm.

explanation: Tests 'treat low-confidence ambiguous findings more cautiously' directly: escalating this specific fixture to DO_NOT_APPROVE would be over-escalation on unconfirmed evidence.
